data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous topicals & wound care_

**Class:** Anticonvulsant used topically for wound healing

## Mechanism of action
- Promotes fibroblast proliferation and collagen deposition, granulation tissue formation; reduces bacterial load and inflammation

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic ulcers: diabetic foot ulcers, trophic ulcers of leprosy, venous and pressure ulcers, burns (Indian practice — supporting evidence from small studies)

## Dose & formulations
- Phenytoin powder/suspension sprinkled on the ulcer bed after cleaning, daily, with dressing

## Adverse effects
- Local burning; systemic absorption from large ulcers (rare toxicity)

## Contraindications
- Phenytoin hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid large areas.

## Viva points
- Cheap adjunct for trophic ulcers in leprosy

_Sources: Khopkar ch.32 (Phenytoin — wound healing). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
